question: How does known-tool retrieval and attached text alignment differ between the preserved v9 archive index and the corrected v9.1 snapshot?
design: Paired descriptive census of the 45 tool-card IDs present in both editions. Query = current display name. Target = same stable tool-card ID in tools.html. Frozen before evaluation, but after authors knew the indexing defect; not preregistered or blinded.

frame.exclusionReason: Venue records were removed and combined product cards were split during correction; no paired target ID exists for these five records.

outcomes: Primary: proportion of 45 target records whose own indexed text contains every query token (case insensitive substring).
Secondary: exact target hit at rank 1 and within top 5; reciprocal rank of first exact target (zero if absent); counts of top-5 hits with aligned target text.
analysis: Identical corrected runtime search function and stable score sorting applied to both frozen indexes. Census totals and paired changes only, no population confidence interval or significance claim.
limits: Two whole-edition snapshots differ in content, extraction and chunking. This comparison does not isolate a causal code-fix effect, evaluate natural user queries or measure Google, AI search, rankings or manipulation efficacy. Tool-name queries are easy and favour title matching; text alignment tests a separate known defect. Same author selected outcomes and implemented corrections.
